body:
### Problem

LSP hover (and presumably other places that render `MarkupContent`/`MarkedString` as markdown, e.g. signature help) displays raw, backslash-escaped CommonMark punctuation instead of resolving the escape sequences. If a language server returns spec-compliant Markdown where e.g. a period is escaped as `\.` (to avoid the line being parsed as an ordered-list item), Neovim shows the literal backslash to the user instead of just `.`.

This is easy to hit in practice: the C# Roslyn language server (`roslyn-language-server`, used via `roslyn.nvim` or the community `csharp_ls`/`omnisharp` configs) converts XML doc comments to Markdown and escapes `.`, `_` and `-` in prose to prevent accidental list/emphasis parsing. The result is that `K` (hover) on virtually any documented C# symbol shows text like:

```
Returns the sum\. See also `Foo\_Bar`\-baz\.
```

instead of

```
Returns the sum. See also `Foo_Bar`-baz.
```

### Root cause

`vim.lsp.util.convert_input_to_markdown_lines()` and the internal markdown handling (`_normalize_markdown`, the deprecated `stylize_markdown`) only extract code fences / apply syntax regions for embedded code blocks - they never resolve CommonMark backslash-escape sequences (`\\`, `\.`, `\_`, `\-`, `` \` ``, `\*`, ...) in the surrounding prose before the lines are written into the floating window buffer.

### Repro (no LSP server needed)

```
nvim --headless -c 'lua
local lines = vim.lsp.util.convert_input_to_markdown_lines({
  kind = "markdown",
  value = "Returns the sum\\. See also `Foo\\_Bar`\\-baz\\.",
})
print(vim.inspect(lines))
' -c "qa"
```

Output:

```
{ "Returns the sum\\. See also `Foo\\_Bar`\\-baz\\." }
```

The backslashes are passed straight through instead of being resolved, so whatever renders these lines (e.g. `vim.lsp.buf.hover()`'s floating window) shows them literally.

### Expected behavior

Backslash-escaped punctuation that is valid per the CommonMark spec (https://spec.commonmark.org/current/#backslash-escapes) should be resolved before being shown to the user, the same way any CommonMark-conformant renderer would - i.e. the hover window should show `Returns the sum. See also `Foo_Bar`-baz.` (escapes inside literal code spans/fences excluded, since those are verbatim).

### Actual behavior

The raw backslash is shown, making hover documentation harder to read (sentences visually end in `\.` etc.).

### Environment

```
NVIM v0.12.5
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.1.1787165859
```

- LSP server: `roslyn-language-server` (Microsoft's C# LSP, via `seblyng/roslyn.nvim`), but the underlying gap is generic - any server emitting escaped Markdown per spec will trigger it.
- `vim.lsp.buf.hover()` with default handler/config (no custom markdown renderer plugin installed).

### Workaround

Currently working around this client-side with a wrapper around `vim.lsp.handlers["textDocument/hover"]` that does a naive `gsub("\\([%.%-_])", "%1")` on `result.contents.value` before calling the default handler. This is good enough for plain prose but isn't a real CommonMark-escape parser (e.g. it would also unescape backslashes that are meant to be literal inside inline code spans).
title: LSP hover shows raw backslash-escaped Markdown punctuation (\., \_, \-) instead of resolving CommonMark escapes
